issue.title: External issue mirror never fires a close transition for an issue that was already closed when first mirrored
issue.description:
Proposed by phase bead sase-k2.4 (epic sase-k2) as a PROPOSED FOLLOW-UP note on 2026-08-12T17:44:55Z, verified in the tree by sase-k2.land at HEAD 67d846327.

MECHANISM (confirmed in source): src/sase/external_mirror/issues.py:326-328 seeds durable state for every ref covered after a pass that has no recorded upstream state — 'for ref, issue in current_refs.items(): if ref in covered_after and ref not in upstream_states: upstream_states[ref] = issue.state'. A bead created this pass is in covered_after (line 323 unions outcome.created_refs), so an upstream issue that was ALREADY closed when the mirror first saw it has 'closed' recorded as its seen state on the very pass that created the bead. _plan_transitions (issues.py:526) compares the new upstream state against that recorded previous_state, so it sees no transition — not on that pass, and never on any later pass.

IMPACT: the mirror creates every bead 'open' (deliberately, so no TaskTriage gate fires on a first-pass backlog). For an issue that closed upstream before SASE ever saw it, that open bead is permanently wrong: sase-k2.4's close/reopen sync cannot correct it because there is no transition to observe. The larger the tracker's closed backlog on first mirror, the more permanently-open beads. Beads whose issue closes AFTER the first sighting are unaffected and close correctly.

SCOPE: this is a creation/filter policy decision, not a bug_status one, which is why sase-k2.4 scoped it out rather than fixing it. The plausible options are mutually exclusive and want a deliberate choice: (a) do not create a bead at all for an issue already closed at first sight — closest to external_mirror.issues.filters.states, which can already express 'states: [open]' but is empty by default; (b) create the bead and immediately close it with the same attributed note the transition path writes; (c) create it open and leave upstream_states[ref] unseeded so the next pass observes a synthetic open->closed transition. Option (a) interacts with the epic's stated superset promise (the bead list is a strict superset of the issue list), so decide that explicitly.

RELEVANT FILES: src/sase/external_mirror/issues.py (_apply seeding at 323-331, _plan_transitions at 512-560), src/sase/default_config.yml external_mirror.issues.filters.states, docs/axe.md external_mirror lane section.

payload.entry: RELATED: sase-kl — both are external-mirror creation/freshness policy gaps left by epic sase-k2; sase-kl is the pull-request-side fetch window, this is the issue-side first-sight state seeding. They touch different modules (issues.py vs pr_sync.py) and can be worked independently.
